sources.title: Public model roster
sources.evidence: Reopened the live unauthenticated roster on October 27, 2026 (HTTP 200). Exact vispark/vision-medium has name Vispark: Vision Medium, owned_by vispark, 1,000,000 context, text/image/audio/video/file inputs, text output, and reasoning/tools features. It contains no physical total or active parameter-count field; supported_sampling_parameters is unrelated. Its created timestamp is May 15, 2024, but this is model metadata, not an explicit exact-variant release announcement.

sources.title: Vision playground and API documentation
sources.evidence: Rechecked the October 27 deployed site and current index-g5phCnAo.js. The native documentation names vispark/vision-medium and small/medium/large selectors, an authenticated paid API, optional continual-learning state, function tools and text/image/audio/video/PDF input. It specifies 1M context and separately limits combined input content to 980,000 tokens. No physical total or active parameter count is published. The weights field carries learned session state; the site does not distribute the base checkpoint.

sources.title: Vision CLv1 model family table
sources.evidence: Reopened the current first-party homepage on October 27, 2026 (HTTP 200). Its exact Model Family row labels Vision CLv1 - Medium 175B, separately from full Vision CLv1 550B and Small 45B. This is a nominal developer specification; the table has no active-parameter column. The proprietary continual-learning presentation links to the same Vispark Lab service.

sources.title: Continual Learning Models: An Introduction to Weight Management
sources.evidence: Freshly retrieved and read the complete indexed primary article on October 27; direct web fetch still timed out and the index reports a crawl from the preceding month. Section 3 describes a modified Transformer and session experience weights. Section 5 says three models were trained from scratch on that architecture; section 6 explicitly lists Vision CLv1 Medium (175B) and says all three are live at Vispark Lab. No separately activated count or dense/MoE classification is supplied. These are later CLv1 specifications, not an original-2024 checkpoint count.

sources.title: Vision AI by Vispark: a foundational Indian multimodal AI
sources.evidence: September 1, 2025 article explicitly offers the API in small, medium and large sizes. Establishes that the Medium product was publicly available by this date, but does not state its first release date. Confirms the Vision family and text/image/audio/video/PDF inputs.

sources.title: Vispark product timeline
sources.evidence: Read the timeline in deployed script index-BgxKNlqk.js. May 15, 2024 is generic Vision chat launch on vansh.one, May 15, 2025 a chat relaunch, and August 29, 2025 the Lab platform launch. None explicitly dates the first release of the Medium variant.

sources.title: Terms of Service, September 26, 2025
sources.evidence: Read the terms in the current deployed site script. Section 2 covers AI tools and other platform services. Section 5 reserves service content, features and functionality to Vispark and licensors and restricts copying, distribution and modification without written consent. Supports descriptive proprietary hosted access; this is not a public model-weight license.

sources.title: A Culturally Aware Multimodal AI Model, July 2024
sources.evidence: Reopened the parameter passages and searched the complete freshly fetched October 27 primary paper. Generic Vision has 175B parameters and a decoder-only Transformer, with no separately stated active count or Medium size label. Its identical total is not the basis for current Medium 175B; its image-generation output is not transferred to the text-output endpoint.

sources.title: A Self-Improving Experiential AI Model a Path to Continual Learning, November 2025
sources.evidence: Reopened the parameter passages and searched the complete freshly fetched October 27 primary report. Its abstract/architecture introduction describes generic Vision Experiential at 250B, whereas its foundational Vision core specifications say 175B. Neither identifies a Medium variant or separately activated count. This version/scope ambiguity does not override the current exact CLv1 Medium 175B family row, and no older architecture/count is transferred.

sources.title: Vision CLv1 evaluation harness
sources.evidence: Freshly fetched the creator's README on October 27 (HTTP 200). This CLv1 evaluation harness identifies Vispark/Vision Large and links the native Lab API; its size options cover the same family, with medium explicitly used for analysis calls. It offers no total or active model count. Its MIT license applies to evaluation code, not model weights.

sources.title: Vision public launch announcement: Small, Medium and Large API availability
sources.evidence: Fresh full original article dated September 1, 2025 is presented as the Vision introduction and explicitly offers immediate API access through Vispark Lab in small, medium and large sizes. It therefore documents the public launch of all three named sizes, not only generic future plans. The separate August 29 Lab platform milestone does not name the sizes, and later CLv1 specifications are not evidence of their 2025 checkpoint sizes.

sources.title: Vispark official timeline: Lab platform launch
sources.evidence: Fresh deployed timeline content identifies August 29, 2025 as Lab launch with 14 models across modalities, without enumerating the Vision sizes. It separately identifies May 15, 2024 as generic Vision chat launch and May 15, 2025 as its relaunch. None overrides the September 1 introduction that explicitly offers the three API sizes.

patch.notes: 175B is the nominal developer-published total for the later Vision CLv1 Medium served at Vispark Lab, described as a modified Transformer. Active parameters and dense/MoE structure remain undisclosed. The API alias has no dated checkpoint or transition history; CLv1 specifications are not backdated to 2024. The September 1, 2025 developer introduction documents the public launch of the Medium API alias; it does not date the later CLv1 transition. The August 29 Lab platform launch does not enumerate the sizes. Context is 1,000,000 tokens with a separate 980,000-token combined-input limit. Continual-learning state files are not publicly released base weights.

summary: Fresh parameter re-audit retains the directly published nominal 175B for current Vision CLv1 Medium; active parameters remain undisclosed after current-source and later-comparison searches. The older generic Vision papers do not establish an exact Medium lineage. Fresh release-date review accepts September 1, 2025 as the documented public launch of the explicitly offered Medium API. The later CLv1 transition remains undated; all thirteen other field assessments are preserved.

parameter_reaudit.outcome: Retain verified nominal total 175B; retain active null/undisclosed after fresh review.
parameter_reaudit.total_assessment: The current AIVOCO exact Medium family row says 175B. Section 6 of the creator technical article independently states Vision CLv1 Medium (175B), describes three models trained from scratch, and places all three at Vispark Lab. Native deployed docs and the API roster identify the medium alias. Retain published nominal precision; an exact tensor census is not required.
parameter_reaudit.active_assessment: Current family specifications, original technical article, API roster and native docs, and creator evaluation harness do not separately report activated parameters. Fresh targeted total/active and arXiv comparison queries did not identify a usable exact-model later original research table. Session experience-weight updates are not an active-parameter count.
parameter_reaudit.lineage_assessment: The older 2024 paper calls generic Vision 175B; the 2025 Experiential paper uses 250B in the abstract/architecture introduction and 175B for the foundational core. Neither names Medium or guarantees unchanged CLv1 architecture. No ancestor count or active-count inference is transferred. Current exact developer family specification supplies the total directly.
parameter_reaudit.access_limitations: The technical article direct web fetch timed out; the complete indexed original was freshly retrieved and read, with a preceding-month crawl reported. Current homepage, roster and creator README fetched HTTP 200. The deployed Lab script and older PDFs were freshly fetched by the parent on October 27 and independently inspected here.
parameter_reaudit.remaining_uncertainty: No separately published active count, precise tensor census, dense/MoE classification or dated alias-transition history is established. The supported 175B nominal total is retained.

accessed_originals.method: direct HTML and linked deployed app bundle

findings: The September 1 publisher introduction contains launch language and immediate native availability for each of the three exact size names.
A separate August 29 platform launch says 14 models, but does not identify these sizes.
Current CLv1 specifications describe a later backend and are not backdated to this API-alias launch.
release_date_reaudit.outcome: Verified 2025-09-01, day precision, as the documented public API-size launch.
limitations: No immutable dated checkpoint or alias transition to later CLv1 is published in the reviewed sources. The public introduction establishes launch; undocumented earlier availability is not inferred.
